notes:
I couldn't write these notes. My first attempt ran ten searches at once and went over the tool's usage limit. After that the tool blocked any further calls for this turn, so I never got to read a single page.

I have no search results or pages to work from, and your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, with a URL for each point. So I haven't drafted anything from memory. Notes built that way would break your sourcing rules and couldn't be cited.

**What I'll do when you ask again**, running searches one or two at a time:
1. **Main verse-by-verse sources:** Enduring Word on Numbers 5, and the Ellicott, Gill and Pulpit Commentary pages on biblehub.com or studylight.org, plus preceptaustin.org.
2. **Protestant traditions:** Wesley's Notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Matthew Henry and Ryle-era material (ccel.org), Reformed and Baptist pieces (thegospelcoalition.org, ligonier.org, desiringgod.org, gty.org), and Lutheran material (lcms.org, 1517.org). These matter most for verses 1–4 (sending unclean people out of the camp), 6–8 (confession and repaying wrongs) and 11–31 (the ordeal).
3. **Other views:** the netbible.org notes on verses 17–28 (the "bitter water," "thigh" and "belly"), bibleodyssey.org on the ordeal, gotquestions.org, and Catholic and Orthodox readings (newadvent.org, catholic.com, oca.org).

Reply "continue" in a new message and I'll do the research and write the notes verse by verse, with a URL on every point.
